uas_topic: Critical infrastructure; schools; agricultural lands; private property/state hunting lands; state preemption
regulated_activity: Flight over/contact with critical infrastructure, schools, agricultural lands, private property, state wildlife management lands
permit_or_approval_required: No (exemption is FAA Part 107 compliance + commercial purpose, not a separate state permit)
summary: Prohibits knowingly/willfully operating a drone over, or allowing contact/interference with, an expanded list of 20 'critical infrastructure facilities' (power, water/wastewater, chemical, seaports, airports, correctional facilities, dams, military installations, etc.) unless the operation is commercial and FAA-authorized (330.41(4)) - 3rd-degree felony if violated. Separately bans overflight/contact with pre-K-12 schools at all times (330.41(5)); bans operation on classified agricultural land without owner consent (330.41(6), new 2025); and bans drone contact with private property/state wildlife management lands/shooting ranges made with intent to harass (330.41(7), new 2025). Vests UAS regulatory authority in the state and preempts most local UAS-specific ordinances (330.41(3)), while preserving local nuisance/harassment ordinances and takeoff/landing authority over locally owned property.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Build the commercial/FAA-authorization basis into your flight-planning checklist for any job near critical infrastructure, and treat pre-K-12 campuses as a hard no-fly without prior written coordination - there's no construction-project carve-out. Flag any site on classified agricultural land for owner-consent documentation before tasking a crew, and keep standard standoff/no-loiter practices near residences and wildlife-management land regardless of intent.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: N/A — no procurement or equipment-selection implication identified
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: The felony-level penalty for critical-infrastructure violations means flight authorization documentation (FAA certificate, commercial purpose, client contract) should be retained in the project file as an affirmative defense record, not just a courtesy. For school-adjacent construction/renovation work, obtain written principal or district consent in advance; verbal coordination is not adequate given the criminal exposure. The 2025 agricultural-lands and harassment-based property provisions are new and largely untested - build consent documentation into standard operating procedure rather than relying on interpretation of 'intent to harass.'
verification_status: Verified directly against current codified statute text
notes: Sunset clause in 330.41(4)(d) ties critical-infrastructure/weaponized-drone provisions to an FAA Section 2209 process; monitor for future sunset. Full critical-infrastructure list has 20 enumerated facility types as of 2025 text - see source for complete list.

source_title: Searches and seizure using a drone (Freedom from Unwarranted Surveillance Act)
uas_topic: Privacy/surveillance restriction; law-enforcement warrant requirement; AEC-relevant exemptions; governmental agency drone security/procurement standards
regulated_party: Law enforcement agencies; any person, state agency, or political subdivision using an imaging-equipped drone; governmental agencies acquiring drones
regulated_activity: Drone-based surveillance/evidence gathering; imaging of private property; government UAS procurement
requirement_type: Prohibition with numerous listed exemptions; procurement restriction
permit_or_approval_required: No permit for private operators relying on an exemption; search warrant required for law enforcement outside listed exceptions
public_agency_only: Partial - subsection (7) procurement rule is public-agency-only; subsection (3)(b) privacy prohibition applies to any person/agency
summary: (3)(a)-(b): bars law enforcement from using a drone to gather evidence without a warrant/exception, and bars any person/agency from using an imaging-equipped drone to surveil private property/persons in violation of a reasonable expectation of privacy without written consent. (4): lists 18 exemptions including (i) property-appraiser ad valorem assessment, (j) utility operations/maintenance/inspection/routing/environmental monitoring, (k) aerial mapping in FAA compliance, (n) communications-service-provider facility work, (g) state/political-subdivision disaster-damage assessment and vegetation/wildlife management on public land, (o) FWC/Florida Forest Service invasive-species and wildfire work. (7): DMS-administered approved-manufacturer list; governmental agencies were required to discontinue non-approved-manufacturer drones by Jan. 1, 2023.
practical_interpretation_aec_expert: Aerial mapping, corridor survey, and utility-inspection flights fall squarely within the (4)(k) and (4)(j) exemptions - tag each flight log with the exemption relied on so it's easy to pull for a client or regulator later. For property-appraiser or public-works contract work, confirm the client agency's own drone equipment (if you're flying theirs) is on the DMS-approved-manufacturer list before you show up with a non-approved airframe.
practical_interpretation_uas_procurement: Before pricing public work involving client-owned or contract-furnished UAS, request the agency's current equipment, insurance, data, and support requirements. Do not assume an internal acquisition policy governs firm-owned aircraft unless the contract incorporates it.
practical_interpretation_legal_counsel: Because the privacy prohibition in (3)(b) carries civil remedies including punitive damages and attorney's fees for the prevailing party, standard operating procedure should require every commercial flight over or near private property to be tied in writing to a specific (4) exemption - not just a general belief that the work is 'mapping.' For any contract with a Florida public agency, confirm in the scope of work whether the agency's own DMS approved-manufacturer requirement is being imposed as a flow-down contract term, since it can affect equipment procurement lead time.
verification_status: Verified directly against current codified statute text
notes: DMS approved-manufacturer list is published on the Department of Management Services website, not in statute; obtain current list before any state-contract UAS work.
